source.title: Hybrid dual-batch and cyclic progressive learning for efficient distributed training of convolutional neural networks
source.authors: Kuan-Wei Lu; D. Hong; Pang-Feng Liu; Jan-Jan Wu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how batch size changes held-out performance using its own ResNet-18 training sweep, a different setup from the cited large-batch work.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports dual-batch and hybrid scheme results, but those compare its proposed recipes; the batch-size sweep in Table 2 directly tests the claim version.
record.test_reason: Table 2 directly measures held-out accuracy and loss across batch sizes under a fixed 95-epoch schedule, testing V5. Homogeneous all-small versus all-large worker configurations provide additional fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors report declining accuracy with increasing batch size in the single-GPU sweep, argue that sufficient small-batch participation improves generalization, and conclude that combining dual-batch learning with cyclic progressive learning reduces training time while maintaining comparable or improved accuracy. These conclusions concern their tested recipes; they do not establish the proposed sharpness mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: A CIFAR-100 ResNet-18 batch-size sweep with a fixed 95-epoch schedule; it does not reproduce the original studies' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Held-out performance varies with batch size; the accuracy decline is monotonic over the tested sweep, while test loss is lower than the batch-32 value at 64–256 and higher at 512–1024.

fits_no_version.finding: Cyclic progressive learning and hybrid recipe comparisons jointly change resolution, batch scheduling and regularization, and report training speed and held-out performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jointly adapting image resolution, batch size and regularization can improve the training speed–accuracy tradeoff.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the batch-size sweep; only one dataset, model, and single-GPU setting are used, and the paper reports test rather than training error in this experiment.
record.rows_left_out: none; Table 2 batch-size sweep results for both test accuracy and test loss are recorded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers and tuning-dependent differences.
Language models, longer-training recovery, learning-rate scaling ablations, and isolated normalization or regularization remedies. Warmup is used, but its effect is not isolated.
An isolated dropout comparison; resolution, batch size and dropout change together in the hybrid recipe.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness, training–test gaps and comparisons with alternative generalization measures. Sharpness appears only in background discussion.
Identification and removal of memorized examples.

missing.what: Homogeneous batch-size comparisons at 140 epochs: all-large batch 500 gives 67.8% accuracy and 1.429 loss; all-small batches 242 and 160 give 70.1%/1.399 and 70.5%/1.415. These endpoints compare uniform batch sizes without mixing worker types.

Updated CIFAR-100 homogeneous comparison at 140 epochs: all-large batch 560 gives 68.0% accuracy and 1.948 loss; all-small batch 286 gives 69.8% and 1.875. Use the fixed-resolution dual-batch-learning block, not the hybrid block.

ImageNet homogeneous comparison at 105 epochs: all-large batch 740 gives 65.9% accuracy and 1.874 loss; all-small batch 236 gives 65.5% and 1.913. Both use fixed resolution 288 and dropout 0.3. Compare raw values directly; Table 12's improvement column uses the hybrid baseline instead.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 values and schedule are correctly extracted. No uncertainty estimates are supplied for its performance comparisons. The study is not an original source for V5. Missing comparisons are restricted to homogeneous all-small versus all-large endpoints; mixed-worker method rankings do not isolate batch size.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization were not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
The batch-size sweep is on CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18 on a single GPU; the paper does not test language models or report training error alongside test error.
No dropout ablation addressing its effect on held-out error.
No trained-network sharpness or generalization-gap measure.
No memorized-example identification or removal experiment.
